# dsh-scratch-vault
**Codex-style scratch execution for DeepSeek Harness — operation scripts run outside the workspace,
and get collected in the plugin.**
English | 中文

A DSH plugin that keeps agent workspaces to deliverables. The throwaway probes,
one-off converters a

nd diagnostics an agent writes only to run once no longer
land in your repository: they execute from

a session scratch root outside the
workspace, and every one of them is archived in a plugin-owned v

ault you can
list, read, promote, or purge.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why

Long-running agent tasks accumulate intermediate files. The files themselves cost
nothing on disk; t

he cost is that every later `glob`, `grep` and directory
listing has to wade through them, which pus

hes irrelevant content into context
and makes the agent re-derive what it already did.

DSH already has most of the machinery to prevent this. Its `workspace-write`
sandbox grants writes u

nder the workspace root **or** a platform temporary root
(`writableRoots` returns the workspace root

, `/tmp` and `os.tmpdir()`), and the
workspace change summary already excludes temporary roots (`isT

emporaryPath` —
"scratch paths that never enter the change summary"). What is missing is the part
th
at routes scratch work there, and the part that remembers it.
This plugin is those two parts.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart DSH. From a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

On Windows use forward slashes in the path, or pnpm will splice the drive letter
into the profile di
rectory and the plugin will install without activating.

Requirements: Node ≥ 22 and a DSH build that mounts the `tools` service. The
plugin declares **no de

pendencies at all** — not even `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`.
A linked plugin's bare specifiers resolve a

gainst its *real* path, which never
reaches the profile's `node_modules`, so one host import is enou

gh to make the
whole plugin fail to load with nothing but `failed to import` to show for it.
Tool de

finitions are therefore assembled by hand in `lib/tools.js`, producing
exactly the shapes `defineToo

l` produces. Nothing to install, nothing to keep in
sync.

Editing any file under `lib/` requires a **full DSH restart**. The loader builds
its module graph at

boot and caches each module by its resolved URL, so
disabling and re-enabling the bundle re-runs th

e cached module's `apply()` — it
does not re-import the file.
## What it does
### L2 — discipline, environment, inline execution

- **A system-prompt section** telling the model that operation scripts belong in
the scratch root, n

ot the workspace.
- **`$DSH_SCRATCH` and `$DSH_VAULT`**, injected into every shell call through
`ctx

.shellEnv`. The namespace is rebuilt per shell call, so the value is always
the calling session's ow

n directory.
- **`run_script({ language, code, description })`** — the "run it without writing
a fil

e into the workspace" tool. The program is written to a scratch file
outside the workspace and execu

ted through `ctx.shell`, so it runs under the
session's sandbox policy. This is the right answer to

"I just need to run
something".
### L3 — interception

`tools/execute` is the only seam that runs *around* dispatch and can therefore
change what a tool bo

dy receives: the registry passes the mutable execution into
the waterfall, and `dispatchToolBody` re

ads `exec.arguments` afterwards.
(`tools/pre-execute` cannot do this — its decision type is
`allow |
deny | cancel | ask`, with no place to put arguments.)

When a `write` or `edit` targets a scratch script inside the workspace, its
`file_path` is rewritten

to the session scratch root, and the tool result tells
the model the real absolute path plus the va

ult entry id. Shell commands that
reference the redirected script are rewritten too.
Two properties keep this safe:

- **The mapping is a pure function of the path** (`scratchPathFor`). DSH
dispatches tool calls in pa

rallel groups, so a `write` and the `pwsh` that runs
it can be in flight simultaneously; anything or

der-dependent would race.
- **A shell token is only rewritten when the workspace file does not exist

.** A
legacy leftover that really is on disk keeps running from disk.

The shell rewriter is deliberately conservative, because a missed rewrite costs one
uncollected file

while a wrong rewrite breaks a command that used to work. A token
is left alone when it sits next t

o a glob metacharacter, extends a longer filename
(`x.py.bak`), is part of a shell variable referenc

e (`$env:X\a.py`,
`$DSH_SCRATCH/a.py`, `%TEMP%\a.py`), or is **relative and its working directory
ca

nnot be determined** — `cd $env:WORK`, `cd %WORK%`, a bare `cd` (which goes to the
home directory),

rmined** — `cd $env:WORK`, `cd %WORK%`, a bare `cd` (which goes to the
home directory), `cd ~/proj`.

A relative token after an earlier `cd`/`Set-Location`/`pushd` is resolved against the
directory that

change put the shell in, not blindly against the workspace root:
`cd <workspace>` then `python _pro

be.py` is the everyday shape and still redirects to
the scratch path the write produced, while `cd …

\lib` then `Get-ChildItem notes.js`
refers to a real file and is left alone. Absolute paths stay una

mbiguous and are
always redirected, drive letter included.

A token is only rewritten in a **program position**: the argument slot of an

### L4 — the vault

Every intercepted script is archived under the vault directory with a JSONL
ledger, plus `scratch_li

st`, `scratch_show`, `scratch_promote` (copy one back
into the workspace as a real deliverable) and

ow`, `scratch_promote` (copy one back
into the workspace as a real deliverable) and `scratch_purge`.

`scratch_import` retrofits residue that was already in the workspace before the
plugin existed: it c

ollects the paths you name, verifies the vault copy
byte-for-byte, and only then removes the origina

l (`keepOriginal: true` keeps it,
`dryRun: true` reports without touching either side). Two guard ra

ils matter here:
it only collects files whose bytes survive a UTF-8 round trip — a lossy decode
